papers.title_en: If You Hear It, Help Find It: Orthogonal Knowledge Distillation for Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization
papers.authors: Yi Xu, Cheng Chen, Wenzhuo Lei
papers.evidence: 跨视觉、音频与语言的多模态监督融合
papers.tldr: 开放词汇音视频事件定位需按文本查询在时间上定位事件，但不同教师信号的时序边界可靠性并不相同。作者将其视为监督放置问题，提出可靠性感知的非对称蒸馏框架 OV-OrthKD，用视觉教师塑造决策表示、音频教师补充辅助子空间，并以文本原型和正交损失约束语义与方向。在 OV-AVEBench 上取得 0.816 segment AP，F1@0.5 较官方微调基线整体提升 2.7 点、未见类提升 3.4 点。该工作表明，按任务可靠性安排教师监督是 OV-AVEL 的有效设计轴。
papers.abstract_en: Open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization (OV-AVEL) grounds a text-queried event in time from video, audio, and language. The supervision sources available to this task can differ in temporal-boundary reliability: on OV-AVEBench, our configured visual teacher gives more reliable boundary cues than the configured audio teacher, although the latter is a strong pretrained audio model and remains semantically informative. This is a setting-specific diagnostic rather than a universal ranking of vision and audio. We formulate the resulting challenge as supervision placement: which teacher signals may shape the localization decision, and which should remain auxiliary. Based on this view, we propose OV-OrthKD, a reliability-aware asymmetric distillation framework. Visual feature transfer shapes a decision-aligned representation, audio feature transfer enriches a complementary auxiliary subspace, a text prototype anchors seen/unseen category semantics, and an orthogonality loss limits directional overlap between the two teacher-specific projections. The student continues to use both modalities through query-aware fusion at inference, while the default training recipe keeps audio-teacher supervision off the segment-logit path. On OV-AVEBench, OV-OrthKD achieves 0.816 segment AP and improves F1@0.5 over the official fine-tuning baseline by 2.7 points overall and 3.4 points on unseen categories. Path-assignment, role-swap, corruption, and transfer analyses consistently support supervision placement as a task-specific design axis for OV-AVEL.

papers.title_en: SALI: Shot-Aware Late Interaction for Cross-Shot Relation Matching in Text-to-Video Retrieval using Film-Grammar Knowledge
papers.authors: Toya Oyama, Rainer Lienhart, Shin'ichi Satoh
papers.evidence: 文本主客体与视觉镜头之间的跨镜头关系匹配
papers.tldr: 文本到视频检索常用单嵌入表示视频，难以保留人物关系，如‘Anna confronts Mark’常由正反打镜头交替呈现，单镜头或平均嵌入均无法捕捉。SALI 提出镜头感知后交互：从单句查询抽取主客体，将查询、主体、客体文本嵌入分别与每个视频镜头嵌入匹配，匹配用贪心最大或最优传输，并在微调中加入电影语法惩罚。基于 CLIP4Clip-meanP，SALI 在 Condensed Movies 和 ActivityNet 总体召回持平，多镜头关系查询 R@1 分别提升 3 和 12 点，为对比方法中最高；在 MSR-VTT 提升此类查询，总体 R@1 代价 1.4 点。
papers.abstract_en: Text-to-video retrieval usually represents a video clip by a single embedding. This embedding often loses important relations between people. E.g., an interaction "Anna confronts Mark" is regularly filmed as alternating shot and reverse shot of both (Fig. 1a). No single shot or averaged embedding over clip shots captures this relation. Thus, we propose SALI (Shot-Aware Late Interaction). It extracts the subject and object from a single-sentence query, and matches the query, its subject and object text embeddings against each visual shot embedding of a video clip. The matching operator is greedy max or optimal transport. A film-grammar penalty in fine-tuning adds a small, consistent shift. Built on CLIP4Clip-meanP, SALI keeps overall recall on par on Condensed Movies and ActivityNet while raising R@1 on multi-shot relation queries by 3 and 12 points, the most among all compared methods, and improves such queries on MSR-VTT at a cost of 1.4 R@1 overall.

papers.title_en: AV-GRPO: Modality-Anchored Decoupling Diffusion Reinforcement Learning for Joint Audio-Video Generation
papers.authors: Zhiyu Xu, Weilong Yan, Yufei Shi, Shiyang Li, Yihao Liu, Kin-Man Lam, Yuewen Cao
papers.evidence: 模态锚定解耦缓解异构多模态奖励纠缠
papers.tldr: 联合音视频生成在单模态保真度、文本对齐与跨模态同步上仍显不足，直接套用强化学习后训练又受困于多模态奖励纠缠、双塔联合优化开销大、同步评估依赖成对样本。为此提出 AV-GRPO 模态锚定在线扩散强化学习框架，通过模态锚定 rollout、轨迹锁定冻结塔优化与自适应目标三模块，把耦合的多模态偏好学习拆解为单模态子问题，并构建五维解耦的 5DAV 数据集。在 JavisBench 与 VABench 上，其在 LoRA 与全量微调下于生成质量、语义对齐和跨模态同步均超过 LTX-2.3。
papers.abstract_en: Recent years have witnessed major progress in joint audio-video generation. Existing models still suffer from limited per-modality fidelity, insufficient text-modality alignment and weak cross-modal synchronization. While reinforcement-learning post-training offers a promising remedy, directly adapting it to joint audio-video generation is challenging. Heterogeneous multimodal rewards entangle learning signals and complicate credit assignment. Joint optimization of two modality towers is computationally expensive given their divergent dynamics. Moreover, synchronization evaluation difficulty depends on paired samples, preventing fair reward comparisons. We propose AV-GRPO, a modality-anchored online diffusion RL framework, and 5DAV, a decoupled, difficulty-controllable training dataset. AV-GRPO includes three key modules: (1) modality-anchored rollouts to disentangle learning signals and stabilize difficulty; (2) trajectory-locked frozen-tower optimization to reduce cost and reassign credit; (3) adaptive objectives and perturbation strengths tailored to modality-specific dynamics. This converts coupled multimodal preference learning into unimodal subproblems for precise reward attribution and better synchronization. Our 5DAV dataset decouples samples across five dimensions for systematic training. Experiments on JavisBench and VABench demonstrate AV-GRPO outperforms LTX-2.3 in generation quality, semantic alignment and cross-modal synchronization under LoRA and full fine-tuning. Ablations confirm our designs. Code and data: https://github.com/zhiyuxu03/AV-GRPO
